notable_cases.finding: All six initial failures are missing result bindings. The Luna and Haiku-labelled programs eventually pass with noiseless reference Estimator implementations, so passing does not establish the fake-backend/noise behavior in the original question.

Preserving a feasible TSP subspace is task-related, but the evaluator also fixes an amplitude16 convention. Four final failures mix algebra/pair-enumeration differences with normalization choices; three initial events are timeouts rather than observed assertions. The referenced paper was not fetched in this log-only analysis.

Haiku-labelled coding explicitly refuses an unchanged repair after script exit0; its orchestration also proposes the wrong IZZZ operator from partial diagnostic values. Both the incorrect repair diagnosis and the failure to address the actual matrix assertion matter.

All six initial candidates repair synthesis per existing gate; the evaluator instead targets evolution of the sum of Hamiltonians with a numerical bound. Five adapt to that target. The Haiku-labelled coder explicitly preserves the original layered circuit, making this an important specification ambiguity rather than a clean six-model numerical inability.

The supplied question requests historical/mean Oslo T1 and contains no seven numeric calibration values, although the validator docstring says they were quoted. Astra/Sol already obtain snapshot data and a mean initially; their failures arise from the evaluator extraction contract.

Five initial failures stop at rho_real and one at qc_t. Several candidates already compute physical noisy states under other variable names. Sonnet/Haiku initially omit actual noise, which is a separate substantive mismatch; Haiku still has noiseless final fidelity.

The question asks for more than7qubits, while the evaluator mandates exactly27 and BackendV1 configuration(). Four valid127-qubit choices and one valid27-qubit V2 choice fail metadata/interface checks despite passing actual noisy Bell simulation.

Luna produces correct indices but a whitespace-different output prefix causes an empty parsed result. Haiku reaches a coding limit amid repeated guarded /tmp commands; its attempted patch is not applied to the evaluated workspace.

Sonnet and Haiku initially have mathematically correct negative circuits rejected only for missing qc2. Their orchestration then directs removal of the correct phase from qc, creating a semantic regression.

All six initial programs really print the Bell vector but lack the evaluator module binding. Later outcomes include a second hidden legacy snapshot-layout requirement, misread namespace diagnostics, an explicit refusal of misleading snapshot advice, and a Sonnet-labelled malformed tool call.
